item.title: Airline Shakeup: Surprising Route Cuts and Bold Expansions
item.description:
What if the airline you fly every month suddenly disappeared from your home airport? For thousands of American travelers this week, that scenario just became reality. The U.S. airline industry is undergoing one of its sharpest reshuffles of 2026 — with one major carrier slashing six routes while a smaller rival adds fourteen new ones across the Caribbean.

Quick Summary: American Airlines is suspending six routes citing high jet fuel costs, hitting eight Florida airports. Meanwhile, BermudAir is launching 14 new Caribbean routes and adding St. Pete-Clearwater to its East Coast network. Alaska Airlines is also tightening basic economy rules and opening a new premium Portland lounge.

item.title: EU Entry-Exit System Delays: What Americans Must Know
item.description:
Imagine arriving at a European airport three hours early, only to still miss your flight home. That nightmare is now playing out across the continent, and the culprit is the EU entry-exit system delays sweeping through major hubs from Milan to Geneva.

Quick Summary: The EU’s new Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational on April 10, 2026. It requires fingerprints and facial photos from all non-EU travelers, including Americans and Britons. Queues are already reaching three hours at peak times. More than 1,600 flights were affected in early April alone, and the Airports Council International has warned the situation will be “simply unmanageable” during peak summer.

item.title: Alaska Airlines' Biggest Expansion Yet: New Routes, Business Class Suites, and a Bold Global Vision
item.description:
What happens when a regional carrier decides to go global? Alaska Airlines is answering that question right now — and the results are turning heads across the aviation industry.

Key Takeaways

  • Alaska Airlines is launching 13 new routes including service to 2 brand-new cities: Tulsa, OK and Arcata-Eureka, CA
  • The airline unveiled its first-ever International Business Class Suites, setting a new standard for long-haul travel
  • All Boeing 787 Dreamliners are getting a new Northern Lights-inspired livery as part of a unified branding strategy
  • A single unified app now covers both Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines
  • San Diego and Portland are emerging as the carrier’s fastest-growing West Coast hubs

Alaska Airlines Route Expansion: 13 New Routes and 2 New Cities

Alaska Airlines is making its most aggressive network push in years. The Seattle-based carrier announced 13 route changes for spring 2026, headlined by nonstop service to two entirely new cities — Tulsa, Oklahoma and Arcata-Eureka Airport (ACV) in Northern California’s Humboldt County.

item.title: TSA Wait Times PHL: Essential Guide to Surviving Philadelphia Airport Security
item.description:
Half of Philadelphia International Airport’s security checkpoints are closed, TSA workers are going without pay, and wait times have stretched past 44 minutes — and that’s on a good day. If you’re flying out of PHL anytime soon, here’s everything you need to know to avoid missing your flight.

Key Takeaways

  • Three of six TSA checkpoints at PHL are closed (Terminals A-West, C, and F) since March 18
  • Arrive 2.5 hours early for domestic and 3.5 hours early for international flights
  • TSA PreCheck is available at Terminals A-East and D/E only
  • ICE agents have been deployed to PHL to help ease security lines
  • About 50,000 TSA workers nationwide have been working without pay for over a month

TSA Wait Times at PHL: What’s Happening Right Now

The partial government shutdown over DHS funding has pushed Philadelphia International Airport into crisis mode. Since March 18, 2026, three of the airport’s six main security checkpoints have been temporarily closed in what the airport describes as an effort to “help optimize operations across other checkpoints.”

item.title: Alaska Air Near-Collision at Newark: Essential Facts About the Alarming Close Call
item.description:
Have you ever wondered just how close two massive jets can get before disaster strikes? On March 18, 2026, the answer was a terrifying 300 feet — roughly the length of a football field — when an Alaska Airlines Boeing 737 and a FedEx Boeing 777 cargo plane nearly collided at Newark Liberty International Airport.

Key Takeaways

  • An Alaska Airlines 737 and FedEx 777 came within 300–325 feet of each other on intersecting runways at Newark Airport on March 18, 2026.
  • Air traffic control instructed the Alaska flight to perform a “go-around” when the plane was just 150 feet off the ground.
  • The NTSB and FAA are both investigating the incident.
  • Newark’s intersecting runway design has been flagged as a recurring safety challenge.
  • Separately, Alaska Airlines is scaling up for its busiest spring break operation ever.

Alaska Air and FedEx: What Happened at Newark

The incident occurred around 8:17 p.m. on Tuesday, March 18, as Alaska Airlines Flight 294 arrived from Portland, Oregon, and FedEx Flight 721 arrived from Memphis, Tennessee. Both planes were attempting to land on intersecting runways at one of the busiest airports in the New York City area.
